slides.title: The Pipeline 🏭
slides.content:
# Processing Text

Unlike NLTK (which is a toolkit), spaCy is a pipeline. You pour text in, and a `Doc` object comes out with linguistic annotations.

```python
import spacy

# Load English model
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

# Process text
doc = nlp("Apple is looking at buying U.K. startup for $1 billion")
```

slides.title: Linguistic Features
slides.content:
# Understanding Syntax 🧩

## Part-of-Speech (POS) Tagging
Is it a Noun? Verb? Adjective?
```python
for token in doc:
    print(token.text, token.pos_)
    # Apple PROPN (Proper Noun)
    # is AUX (Auxiliary Verb)
```

## Named Entity Recognition (NER)
Finds real-world objects like companies, countries, dates.
```python
for ent in doc.ents:
    print(ent.text, ent.label_)
    # Apple ORG
    # U.K. GPE
    # $1 billion MONEY
```

slides.title: Word Vectors
slides.content:
# Similarity 👯

Using medium/large models (`en_core_web_md`), spaCy provides word vectors.

```python
doc1 = nlp("I like apples.")
doc2 = nlp("I like oranges.")

print(doc1.similarity(doc2)) # High score (e.g. 0.95)
```
